polls.text: Do you intend to contribute on LOCMAF?
I'm willing to go do the work in MPEG if that's where it is (if not contributing, say No Opinion)

chat.author: Alan Frindell
chat.text: Vienna!

chat.author: Lorenzo Miniero
chat.text: https://moq.conf.meetecho.com/ietf127-moq/

chat.author: Jonathan Lennox
chat.text: And thank you Lorenzo for having a mute button on the moq-in-moq page, for those of us in the room.

chat.author: Lorenzo Miniero
chat.text: I already noticed a tiny bug with slides, if they disappear try refreshing :grinning_face_with_smiling_eyes:

chat.author: Jonathan Lennox
chat.text: Are you video'ing the slides, or do you have a way of sending PDF over MoQ?

chat.author: Chris Lemmons
chat.text: I'll be in the room before the C4M presentation. I've got a conflict on COSE, but my COSE presentation will be done in the top half.

chat.author: Lorenzo Miniero
chat.text: Slides are the same triggers the main tool uses, JSON with a link to an image + slide number

chat.author: Ted Hardie
chat.text: That sounds very sensible.

chat.author: Ted Hardie
chat.text: The draft's contents can completely change if circumstances differ. Adopting the draft really means "we will work on the topic."  But that may not be clear to MPEG.

chat.author: Victor Vasiliev
chat.text: (just got back to a PC where I can use remote tool) for what it's worth, I am still heavily skeptical that LOCMAF adds enough over LOC and CMAF for us to pursue it at this point

chat.author: Ali Begen
chat.text: If CMAF 4th edition has locmaf-like headers, CMSF can simply use that version and get done with it.

chat.author: Ali Begen
chat.text: @victor, the gain is only for very low bitrate streams (so mostly cmaf audio).

chat.author: Victor Vasiliev
chat.text: I understand that; I do not understand the contexts in which you'd use LOCMAF but not LOC

chat.author: Ali Begen
chat.text: if you still need DRM for example, LOCMAF would give you that

chat.author: Magnus Westerlund
chat.text: There are also codecs that has CMAF suppport that are not in the WebCodecs.

chat.author: Magnus Westerlund
chat.text: and thus supported by LOC

chat.author: Ali Begen
chat.text: yup, codec support is much larger in cmaf than WC.

chat.author: Victor Vasiliev
chat.text: IIRC we had a plan for default pub priority at last interim, but it was blocked on subgroup properties?

chat.author: Alan Frindell
chat.text: The slow subscriber text conflicts with TOO_FAR_BEHIND in the core draft?

chat.author: Martin Duke
chat.text: does it mean upstream?

chat.author: Victor Vasiliev
chat.text: I imagine it's one per sub, since you can have many subs for a track now

chat.author: Lorenzo Miniero
chat.text: I guess that a fill FETCH makes a lot of sense on the first SUBSCRIBE/PUBLISH, but after that I agree with Mike that you can just FETCH, no need for a REQUEST_UPDATE with a different fill FETCH

chat.author: Victor Vasiliev
chat.text: FILL FETCH is like a connected UDP socket

chat.author: Mo Zanaty
chat.text: Fill avoids the fetch overhead if subscribed.

chat.author: Colin Perkins
chat.text: We spent a lot of time defining and registering RTP header extensions, payload types and parameters for codecs, etc. Reusing that effort, rather than gradually redefining all the parameters, might make sense.

chat.author: Magnus Westerlund
chat.text: I think going over what exists and it if makes sense at all to expose them to the relay then define them as public properties.

chat.author: Jonathan Lennox
chat.text: Also a fair number of RTP header extensions do things that are handled by the MoQ group structures, and thus I would think wouldn't be necessary.

chat.author: Colin Perkins
chat.text: Fair. The payload formats are likely more reusable.

chat.author: Mo Zanaty
chat.text: Maybe we should proactively look at RTP header extensions used in WebRTC specs rather than the full universe. These may also map well to WebCodecs properties. But this reduced space is still quite large compared to LOC properties today.

chat.author: Magnus Westerlund
chat.text: I am not that certain that it is that many properties that actually make sense to transfer assuming that your goal is not to have a B2B gateway between the systems.

chat.author: Will Law
chat.text: Group numbers are not part of the MOQ claim in C4M

chat.author: Alan Frindell
chat.text: Will: how does "you can't go back" work then?  It forbids FETCH?

chat.author: Mo Zanaty
chat.text: RTP-MOQ B2B GW seems likely in many systems.

chat.author: Will Law
chat.text: FETCH is authorized as an action, independently of Subscribe. But there is no current way of saying you can fetch groups 1-10 but not 20-30.

chat.author: Magnus Westerlund
chat.text: Mo, there is a huge difference between replicating the whole of RTP/RTCP capabilities over the GW rather than having the GW present the relevant information in the systems. I think a lot can be translated, rather then just copied naively.

chat.author: Rohan Mahy
chat.text: If you want to decode/view/manipulate web tokens, including CAT/C4M feel free to use:

chat.author: Rohan Mahy
chat.text: https://rohanmahy.github.io/credential-playground/

chat.author: Mo Zanaty
chat.text: Is fill considered a fetch action? Fill from current group to join vs fetch the entire track seem like very different actions that may need different auth.

chat.author: Slackmoq
chat.text: englishm: Please retest moq-ng at draft-18, draft-22, and draft-23 :slightly_smiling_face:

chat.author: Slackmoq
chat.text: afrind: Reminder that messages in this channel get echo’ed into zulip and show in the session’s chat

chat.author: Gaurab Upadhaya
chat.text: +1 on both

chat.author: Alan Frindell
chat.text: Will: yeah I had the same question as Mo regarding fill fetch.  I think you should express this as "how far behind Largest Object are you allowed" ?

chat.author: Will Law
chat.text: @Alan @MO - agree with you both. We wrote C4M before fill-fetch existed. we need to update.

chat.author: Will Law
chat.text: N back from largest might be a useful limit to enforce.

chat.author: Alan Frindell
chat.text: Seems like you might get a lot of acks, but I guess they just ride in the quic ack packet?

chat.author: Alan Frindell
chat.text: can probably compress them since 99% of the time it's object ID+1 or group+1, object=0

chat.author: Cullen Jennings
chat.text: It seems like a design more like RTCP Feedback would be better

chat.author: Cullen Jennings
chat.text: Like draft-liu-moq-feedback-01

chat.author: Alan Frindell
chat.text: transport ack != app ack

chat.author: Martin Duke
chat.text: Webtrans APIs are even less likely to give you QUIC ACKs

chat.author: Alan Frindell
chat.text: pfff browsers

chat.author: Alan Frindell
chat.text: .session track/s ?

chat.author: Jordi Cenzano
chat.text:
That seems a duplication of effort since QUIC already does this
Also depending on the app it can be implemented using current MOQT
